item.description: I just watched an 'inclusive', Democratic party coalition member show unwavering commitment to 'diversity' by calling out a racial slur on a Black ICE agent during a protest.

item.title: Dr. Umar Johnson Says Black Immigrants Are the Real Targets of Deportation
item.description: 'Pan African nationalist' Dr. Umar Johnson has an interesting take on President Trump's deportation program. The good doctor posits a theory in a video clip that the real immigration targets of the administration aren't Latinos, the favored workforce of those I call 'cheap labor lobby' conservatives quietly supporting mass migration alongside progressives.

item.title: Skiers First To Plow Up Controversy At Olympics
item.description: It was only a matter of time before someone started voicing their opinions on topics they know little about. The odds were in favor of an American being the first to initiate this complaint fest. As expected, two American skiers, along with one who used to ski for the U.S. but now competes for Great Britain, did just that.

item.title: The Left Really Wants Aggressive Black Foot Soldiers In Its Ideological War
item.description: As a 'safety creator', I have an affinity for citizen mobilization, everything from my volunteer safety escorts to subtle neighborhood watch, up to legally armed street patrols in the Black community, and elsewhere too. This affinity comes with guardrails, especially when it appears an outside ideology is the mobilization's beneficiary, instead of securing the community.

item.title: SAVE Act Is Not a Voter ID Law
item.description: Jessica Tarlov’s repeated claim onThe Five (Fox News program) that the SAVE Act would force voters to “show their birth certificate or passport at the polls” is flat‑out false. Whether she’s misinformed or deliberately misleading viewers, the text of the bill does not say what she insists it does. During the segment, Tarlov argued: “…what the SAVE Act does is that it requires that you have either your birth certificate or your passport…”

item.title: Nuclear Energy Rejuvenation
item.description: Global momentum is building around nuclear energy with the International Atomic Energy Agency estimating that the world’s nuclear power capacity could more than double by 2050. In the US, a 2023 survey showed 57 percent want more nuclear plants, up from 43 percent in 2020. During the same period, support for nuclear in the Netherlands grew by half, with twice as many proponents now as opponents.

item.title: Democrats Fight Immigration Enforcement To Have A Future﻿
item.description: About a week ago, the Trump administration announced the withdrawal of 700 Federal Agents from Minnesota. This came as Immigration Czar Tom Holman went there to announce the drawdown and willingness to work with state and local political leaders. These gestures were met by heightened efforts to impede immigration enforcement.
